title: GeoVac (The Geometric Vacuum): Structurally Sparse Qubit Hamiltonians and the Discrete Spectral Triple
description:
GeoVac is a spectral-graph-theory framework for computational quantum chemistry and mathematical physics. Its lattice is the finite label set (n,l,m) of the S^3 hyperspherical harmonics, on which the S^3 Laplace-Beltrami operator acts exactly as the diagonal SO(4) Casimir n^2-1 at every cutoff; Fock's 1935 conformal projection makes that continuum operator equivalent to the hydrogen Schrodinger equation (Paper 7, 18 symbolic checks of the continuum chain). The lattice's edge Laplacian does not converge to the S^3 Laplacian; that is a documented negative result.

The angular-momentum (Gaunt) selection rules of the hyperspherical harmonic basis enforce block-diagonal electron-repulsion integrals, producing qubit Hamiltonians whose Pauli count is exactly linear in the qubit count across molecules at fixed basis (N_Pauli = 27.90 x Q main-group, 30.03 x Q d-block): 51x-317x fewer Pauli terms than Gaussian baselines at equal qubits for H2O (n_max = 1-3), and 76x fewer than cc-pVDZ for LiH (Papers 14, 20). These comparisons are at matched qubit counts, not matched accuracy; against minimal-basis STO-3G, LiH is unfavourable on raw counts. A 37-system library (35 composed molecules plus He and H2) exports to OpenFermion, Qiskit and PennyLane.

Classical validation: He at 0.022% (2D variational, zero free parameters; Paper 13) and H2 at 99.97% of the dissociation energy (prolate explicit-r12 CI with exact integrals; Paper 12). Composed-geometry accuracy is below production quantum chemistry (equilibrium bond length errors of 5.3% for LiH and 19.4% for water; Paper 17); the tool is a research instrument, not a replacement for production quantum chemistry.

On the mathematical side: state-space Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the truncated Camporesi-Higuchi spectral triples on S^3 is proved for the commutative factor only, with the almost-commutative extension open (Paper 38); an annihilation theorem shows that compressing a Krein-self-adjoint product Dirac operator to the Krein-positive subspace makes the compressed Lipschitz seminorm vanish (Paper 45; the earlier Lorentzian convergence claim is retracted, see docs/claims_register.md); the identified S^3 spectral-zeta and heat-trace transcendentals sit in pure-Tate and level-4 cyclotomic mixed-Tate periods (Paper 55); the radial core of the three-centre electron-repulsion integral is an elliptic Bessel moment (Paper 59); and on its one-scale slice a tree of n linked two-centre densities is annihilated by an order-n operator already known from Bessel moments and banana Feynman integrals, checked for n = 2 to 5: elliptic at n = 2, a K3 surface at n = 3, entry #58 of the Calabi-Yau tables at n = 4, nothing new at n = 5 (Paper 63; the operators are prior art, and the general reading, that the shape of the density graph sets the class, is stated as a bounded conjecture).

The repository preserves its negative results and retractions; docs/claims_register.md lists every headline claim with its verification tier and falsifier. No claim is externally peer-reviewed. Developed with an AI-augmented agentic research workflow; results are validated against analytical benchmarks and symbolic check suites.
